summary.text: William Timmons is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for South Carolina's 4th District, in office since January 2019 and seeking re-election. A former prosecutor and small business owner, he served in the South Carolina Senate from 2016 to 2019 and is a captain and Judge Advocate General officer in the South Carolina Air National Guard. In Congress he sits on the Financial Services and Oversight committees.

paragraphs.text: Timmons was born in Greenville, South Carolina, in 1984. He earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University (2006), master's degrees from the University of South Carolina (2009) and New York University (2021), and a law degree from the University of South Carolina (2010).

He owned a small business and worked as a prosecutor in the Thirteenth Circuit Solicitor's Office, and he serves as a captain and Judge Advocate General (JAG) officer in the South Carolina Air National Guard.

Timmons won the 2016 Republican primary runoff for South Carolina State Senate District 6, defeating incumbent Michael Fair with 65.3 percent, and won the November 2016 general election. He served in the State Senate until 2019.

In 2018 he won the Republican primary runoff for the open 4th District seat over Lee Bright (54.3 percent to 45.7 percent), then won the November general election over Democrat Brandon Brown with 59.6 percent. He succeeded Trey Gowdy and took office January 3, 2019.

In the House, Timmons serves on the Financial Services Committee, including its Digital Assets subcommittee, and on the Oversight Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Military and Foreign Affairs and sits on the Delivering on Government Efficiency subcommittee. His earlier House service included the Select Committee on the Modernization of Congress and the House Republican Steering Committee.
He won the June 9, 2026, Republican primary with 65.8 percent over David Atchley and Robert Lee.
